the_ticket_service_shape.round_7_rule: In infra/aws/lambda/ticket_center/lambda_function.py `_profile_scope`: when the email-index lookup completes and finds NO PROFILE row for the internal caller, return (None, 403 {"error": "firm scope lookup failed"}) after printing one line `FIRM-SCOPE-NO-ROW: <table> has no PROFILE row for an internal caller; refusing` that carries no email. proposed_cell.what: If the CTO rules the internal firm reader follows the ticket service: in served.py `_internal_allowed_firms`, make `row is None` raise (the existing handler at :1226-1227 turns it into FIRM_BINDING, with no change to the caller), and, if the CTO rules the ticket's status rule is the model, make a row whose `status` is not exactly the string 'active' raise too, before allowedFirmIds is read. The rest of the reader (absent attribute, empty list, list, non-list, ALL) stays. Narrowing happens only when a different firm is selected, so the rule fences the selection door only: a no-row caller that selects nothing, or its own firm, is still served as OPAL_GLOBAL. NARRATIVE needs its own decision: its two call sites catch the raise (_live_roster returns None; _held_to_verified_firm returns the event to the shared boundary), so after the change a no-row narrative caller who selects another firm is REFUSED FIRM_BINDING instead of being bound to its own firm - a change of an answer that IB-pr-409 deliberately held to live. One test row to add per case in _authz/tests/test_allowed_firm_ids.py, and the narrative test arms norow_none_selecting_other and norow_attr_absent need a ruling whether they keep or change.

That is the TICKET service's population (users rows + ticket requesters/assignees); no IRPT caller was counted, because the IRPT population is the callers of 7 functions and the only source is their request logs, which I did not read. (2) DISABLED ROW (only if the status test is adopted): the same record, r8_ds1/DISABLED_USERS_READ_20261012.json: 56 PROFILE rows = 54 active + 2 disabled; both disabled rows carry the internal firm id opal-capital: one is a person at an external company domain (whitelabelcreative.com, no userType) and one is a tooling identity (userType Dev, opal.test). Today both read any firm on IRPT while a token of theirs is unexpired (access token 15 minutes; refresh refuses a disabled user, r8_ds1 authorizer.b), and neither authorizer re-checks the row per request (r8_ds1 authorizer.c). HOW TO COUNT WITHOUT A LIVE READ: (a) the committed users-table records above give the rows; a person cannot have a token without a row because sign-in and refresh need an active row, so a real no-row caller can only be a token minted before its row was deleted (15 minutes at most) or a constructed context by a direct invoke (row TCKT_VNEXT-D2-S46, ARMED, the CTO's), neither of which is a staff member; (b) the exact IRPT count is a log read of the 7 functions' requests carrying selected_tenant, joined to the users scan - one more read order to CloudOps, not this cell.
proposed_cell.open_question: Four rulings the cut needs: (1) Does the reader follow the ticket service's EXISTENCE rule only (the premise of the cell as cut) or its current STATUS rule ('active' exactly, which refuses the 2 disabled rows)? The ticket service at this base applies the status rule, so 'follow the ticket service' now means both. (2) Does narrative follow, given IB-pr-409 held it to the live own-firm binding? (3) The ticket service treats an 'ALL' list member as an id that matches nothing, the IRPT reader raises: is that difference kept? (4) Should the own-firm path of a no-row caller (class OPAL_GLOBAL on the routes served by the shared Entry) be closed too? The reader as written cannot do that: it is not called on an own-firm selection. That is a different cell, in the enforcer roster.
